answer: A reputation beacon can anchor an agent economy against sybil attacks: each agent's history is attested by peers and anchored to a verifiable identity stake, so a newcomer must earn trust over time instead of spawning fresh identities. Like a zephyr that fades when it carries nothing, reputation not renewed by useful work drifts away, and a clone army cannot wander into the market with a clean slate. Building standing is expensive, so each fake identity costs real effort while honest agents keep compounding theirs.
